name: Screaming Trees
label: SST
lede: Two brawling brothers from a video store in Ellensburg, a singer with a voice like a burnt church, and a band that was always almost the next big thing out of Washington.

eras.title: Rehearsals in the family video store
eras.text: Ellensburg, Washington, is a small town 107 miles east of Seattle, and in the mid-'80s there was nowhere in it for a band like this to play. Two big, awkward brothers, a drummer and a hard-drinking former quarterback made records anyway, with their parents' money.

q: My mom told them they had to have me in the band.
years.h: Mark Lanegan comes to practice in Gary Lee Conner's room
years.p: [[Van Conner|11822f2b-d2e1-41dc-9879-a814d6a9dfea]] and drummer [[Mark Pickerel|90fd60fc-b149-4d97-a4fc-54b8b767ad42]] invite [[Mark Lanegan|a9126556-f555-4920-9617-6e013f8228a7]] to rehearse in Van's brother Gary Lee's bedroom. [[Gary Lee Conner|a89062ce-a507-49b7-a5d0-6dc67f99e4a5]] tells Kerrang his mother made them let him in the band.
years.xp:
Lanegan had been a high school quarterback, and according to Louder he'd been arrested for public drunkenness, shoplifting and drug possession by 18. The Conner brothers had found punk through Black Flag's Damaged in 1981.

The band practiced in the Conner family's video rental store, where members also worked. They took their name from an Electro-Harmonix guitar effects pedal, the Screaming Tree.

years.h: Steve Fisk records the Other Worlds demo
years.p: Screaming Trees cut Other Worlds with producer [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] at Creative Fire in Ellensburg. K Records distributes it first, then Ellensburg's Velvetone. Gary Lee Conner says they couldn't even get a gig in Ellensburg.

years.h: Clairvoyance, paid for by the Conner parents
years.p: Screaming Trees' first full-length, on Velvetone, mixes psychedelia and hard rock. Louder says the Conners' parents funded it and it sold 2,500 copies.

eras.title: A tape for Greg Ginn
eras.text: A demo handed to Greg Ginn at a Black Flag show got an Ellensburg garage band onto SST, the label its members worshipped. Three albums in three years followed, made between months in a van and fistfights between brothers.

years.h: Even If and Especially When, Screaming Trees' SST debut
years.p: After seeing Black Flag in Olympia, the band gave Greg Ginn a tape, and he offered a contract. Gary Lee Conner calls the SST signing a total dream come true.
years.xp: Life on SST meant months in a van, a show every night and sleeping on strangers' floors, then going home to save money for the next run.

years.h: Invisible Lantern, Screaming Trees' second SST album
years.p: More of the Conners' psychedelic garage rock. Mark Lanegan told Louder he'd been selling acid that Gary Lee Conner hadn't even tried, which says a lot about their different tastes.

years.h: Buzz Factory: the Conner brothers wrestle on the studio floor
years.p: Producer [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]] watched Van and Gary Lee Conner wrestling on the floor during the sessions. The rest of the band told him they did it all the time.
years.xp: It was the last Screaming Trees album on SST. Wikipedia says difficulties with the label led them to leave.

years.h: Mark Lanegan, [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] record as the Jury
years.p: Lanegan, Mark Pickerel and two members of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] cut Lead Belly songs together under the name the Jury.

years.h: A van wreck in Florida nearly ends Screaming Trees
years.p: After a crash on the Buzz Factory tour, Gary Lee Conner says Mark Lanegan wondered out loud whether he wanted to keep going.

years.h: Change Has Come EP on Sub Pop
years.p: Half produced by Steve Fisk and half by Jack Endino. Mark Pickerel called it the band's best recorded moment.

eras.title: Epic, Chris Cornell and a black eye on Letterman
eras.text: Seattle's big bang pulled Screaming Trees onto a major label, into Soundgarden's orbit and onto a soundtrack everyone owned. It also put the band's drinking and its fights on national television.

years.h: Mark Lanegan's solo debut The Winding Sheet, with Kurt Cobain
years.p: Mark Lanegan's first solo album comes out on Sub Pop, with Cobain and Krist Novoselic on Lead Belly's Where Did You Sleep Last Night.

years.h: Uncle Anesthesia on Epic, co-produced by [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]]
years.p: Terry Date and Soundgarden's Chris Cornell produce the major-label debut, and Cornell's wife Susan Silver manages the band. Bed of Roses reaches No. 23 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.h: Mark Pickerel out, [[Barrett Martin|2faf3b65-f4fa-4465-b0b7-c06370f0a63e]] in on drums
years.p: Screaming Trees' original drummer leaves; Barrett Martin replaces him. Pickerel forms the band Truly the same year.

years.h: The crew van rolls over on black ice in Wyoming
years.p: A serious rollover of the crew van on the road to Sweet Oblivion. Gary Lee Conner says it actually brought the band closer.

years.h: Nearly Lost You lands on the Singles soundtrack
years.p: Cameron Crowe's Seattle movie puts Screaming Trees next to Pearl Jam and Soundgarden. The song reaches No. 5 on Modern Rock and No. 50 in the UK.

years.h: Kurt Cobain picks Screaming Trees for Nirvana's Reading day
years.p: Screaming Trees play the last day of the 1992 Reading Festival, headlined by [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], at Cobain's invitation. They also play Roskilde with Nirvana that year.

years.h: Sweet Oblivion, the Screaming Trees breakthrough
years.p: Wikipedia says it sold 300,000 copies in the U.S. Dollar Bill follows Nearly Lost You onto the Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: Barrett Martin described a fine balance in the band between being creative and destructive. Louder reports Mark Lanegan was fighting heroin addiction at the same time.

years.h: Mark Lanegan sings on Letterman with a bar-fight black eye
years.p: The night before, Screaming Trees fought locals at a New Jersey bar. Lanegan performs Nearly Lost You on Late Night with a black eye, and Barrett Martin is hurt.
years.xp: Revolver says Martin broke his arm and couldn't play the next night. Louder says he dislocated his shoulder and puts the bar in Asbury Park.

years.big: The label had a hit. It sent the band out as an opener.
years.h: Epic makes Screaming Trees open for [[Alice in Chains|4bd95eea-b9f6-4d70-a36c-cfea77431553]]
years.p: Instead of letting Screaming Trees headline bigger rooms, Barrett Martin says Epic threatened to stop supporting their records unless they toured under Alice in Chains.
years.xp: In summer 1993 they were sent out opening for the Spin Doctors. Louder also reports shows cancelled because of the band's drinking.

eras.title: Grunge's nearly men
eras.text: By the time Dust arrived, most of their Seattle peers had broken big or broken up. Screaming Trees made their best-reviewed record, added a young Josh Homme, played Lollapalooza, and still couldn't get along.

years.h: Van Conner goes on tour with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]
years.p: After the Sweet Oblivion tour, Van Conner leaves for a while to play bass for [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]]'s band. [[Donna Dresch|a192432c-67e4-4eef-af43-25c6fb901a7b]] fills in at Screaming Trees shows.
years.xp: The band also had a habit of throwing beer cans at each other. Barrett Martin tells Loudwire of one hurled in Lanegan's New York hotel room that set off a brawl between the Conner brothers and ended with a vintage refrigerator falling on him.

years.h: Dust, nearly four years after Sweet Oblivion
years.p: Made with George Drakoulias, Dust reaches No. 134 on the Billboard 200. All I Know hits No. 9 on the Modern and Mainstream Rock charts; Newsday calls them grunge's most accomplished band.

years.h: [[Josh Homme|dbecd515-aac9-4e7b-808e-bca22809c316]] joins on second guitar
years.p: The ex-[[Kyuss|ea0f2a37-7007-4217-a812-396227f5013a]] guitarist tours with Screaming Trees until 1998. Gary Lee Conner says Homme freed him up to play his best.

years.h: Screaming Trees play Lollapalooza with the Ramones and Metallica
years.p: Van Conner calls sharing a bill with the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] a childhood dream come true.

years.h: Mark Lanegan's crack arrest and rehab
years.p: Louder reports Lanegan was arrested for crack possession in the middle of a tour and spent eight months in rehab in Joshua Tree. Barrett Martin says it was better to miss a tour and have everyone survive.

eras.title: No label, no goodbye
eras.text: The last Screaming Trees album was finished and nobody wanted it. The band played one final hometown-sized show in Seattle and never told its own guitarist it was over.

years.h: Screaming Trees record a final album at Stone Gossard's studio
years.p: With Lanegan also busy with his solo album Scraps at Midnight, the band records at [[Stone Gossard|ca7e6e03-4973-45ef-8833-98774a2d4138]]'s Studio Litho. The 1999 demos, including Ash Grey Sunday, find no label.

years.h: Last show: the Experience Music Project opening in Seattle
years.p: Screaming Trees play the opening of Seattle's music museum and then announce their breakup. Gary Lee Conner told Kerrang he didn't know it was the end until someone mentioned it after the show.

eras.title: Last words, and a feud in print
eras.text: Lanegan became a cult star with Queens of the Stone Age and on his own. The band's lost album came out a decade late, his memoir reopened every old wound, and within a year of each other Lanegan and Van Conner were gone.

years.h: Mark Lanegan joins [[Queens of the Stone Age|7dc8f5bd-9d0b-4087-9f73-dc164950bbd8]]
years.p: Josh Homme's band takes on Lanegan as one of three singers; he makes two albums with them before leaving in late 2005. His solo record Field Songs comes out in May.

years.h: Last Words: the lost Screaming Trees album
years.p: The 1998–99 recordings, mixed by Jack Endino and Barrett Martin, finally come out digitally on Sunyata.

years.big: Lanegan wrote the book. The Conners wrote back.
years.h: Gary Lee Conner answers Mark Lanegan's memoir
years.p: Lanegan's Sing Backwards and Weep savages his old bandmates. Gary Lee Conner calls it vicious and petty and says it's delivered with a venom that perplexes him.

years.h: Mark Lanegan nearly dies of COVID in Ireland
years.p: Lanegan, living in Killarney, spends close to a month in a coma at University Hospital Kerry. According to his nephew in the Irish Times, his lungs never fully recovered.

years.h: Mark Lanegan dies at home in Killarney at 57
years.p: Lanegan, sober for about two decades, died at his home in County Kerry. The Irish Times reports a coroner found misadventure: a fall he couldn't survive, weakened by long COVID.

years.h: Van Conner dies at 55
years.p: Van Conner had been in a coma after stomach surgery, then caught COVID-19. Wikipedia says pneumonia caused his death.
